tests.name: Effective description
tests.message: Verdict not allowed for this test: 'warning' (allowed: passed, failed)

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps directly into project-specific semantics (evidence tiers, push correlation rule, verdict model, required permissions) without explaining general concepts like what ECR or lifecycle policies are. All content is domain-specific and non-obvious.
tests.evidence: "Tier (a) and tier (b) evidence is used as found. Tier (c) is used only after the push correlation rule below."

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed tables (permissions, verdict model, check matrix, quirks) are concise summaries rather than exhaustive API docs; the truly large reference material (API error classification, full simulation procedure, report skeletons) is pushed out to references/ files loaded conditionally at specific steps.
tests.evidence: "Load [ecr-api-reference.md](references/ecr-api-reference.md) now." / "Load [ecr-lifecycle-semantics.md](references/ecr-lifecycle-semantics.md) and run its numbered procedure exactly"

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All three reference files are linked via markdown links in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is tied to a specific trigger/step telling the agent when to load it.
tests.evidence: "Load [ecr-api-reference.md](references/ecr-api-reference.md) now." and "Load [ecr-lifecycle-semantics.md](references/ecr-lifecycle-semantics.md) and run its numbered procedure exactly: ... Step 4 (only if Step 3 did not complete)."

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, failure-prone operations (push correlation rule, preview/approval flow, verdict precedence) are given exact prescriptive rules, while flexible areas (scope resolution, protective rule wording) explain intent and allow reasonable judgment, matching specificity to fragility.
tests.evidence: "A `BatchGetImage`, ... event whose `eventTime` is within 60 seconds of that image's `imagePushedAt` is part of the push workflow and MUST NOT count as a consumer pull."

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill designates a clear default (preview via StartLifecyclePolicyPreview) with a documented fallback (deterministic simulation) rather than presenting multiple equal options.
tests.evidence: "Preview is the source of truth. Try `StartLifecyclePolicyPreview` on every run. Only when it cannot complete, simulate..."

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable procedure (scope resolution, evidence hierarchy, verdict rules, checklist) that applies to any repository/policy combination, not a one-off instance; the extensive example in 'Why This Skill Exists' is used as illustrative evidence, not as the actual task instructions.
tests.evidence: "Step 6. Cross reference every expiring image, tier by tier. Match by digest and by every tag (through the tag to digest map) against every reference in the inventory."

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has an extensive 'Known Quirks' table documenting concrete, non-obvious environment-specific facts (e.g., push events masquerading as pulls, refresh delays, ANDed tag lists) that directly address mistakes the agent would otherwise make.
tests.evidence: "An image push emits `BatchGetImage` (and layer events) 1 to 2 seconds after `imagePushedAt`, from the pushing principal (observed 2026-10-27 on 26 of 26 images) | The push correlation rule drops these events..."

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill explicitly provides a report-template.md reference for structured output, satisfying the need for templates in a report-generating skill.
tests.evidence: "The only acceptable output is the report defined in [report-template.md](references/report-template.md)."

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large output template is embedded inline in the body; the full report skeleton is kept in references/report-template.md and only column names/headings are listed in the body.
tests.evidence: "Expiring Images columns: Tags, Digest (first 12 hex characters), Pushed, Last recorded pull, Claimed by rule, Action, Verdict, Evidence."

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The Execution Flow section presents an ordered, dependent procedure using the required checkbox checklist format with 'Step N' naming, and subsequent detailed content (e.g., push correlation rule references Step 6) ties back to those steps.

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit self-check instruction requiring the agent to verify its own output for internal consistency before sending.
tests.evidence: "Self check before responding. The expiring image count must be identical in Scope, Source of Truth, Expiring Images and the Rule by Rule total. ... If any of these fail, fix the report before sending."
